place: A ridge overlooking a wooded valley, well after dark, no moon.
lines: climb the ridge and look for anyone camped in the valley
outcome: From the ridge the player sees a small orange glow through gaps in the trees, far off but unmistakable against the dark valley floor. By day the same fire would show only as a thin haze of smoke, harder to place and easy to mistake for mist. The player can guess roughly where the camp is but not how many people are there or what they are doing.

effects: player learns a fire is in the valley
numbers: how far a small flame is visible at night from elevation

latent: how many people are at the fire
state_after: campfire: burning, visible at night from the ridge
player: aware of a distant camp, direction only
stress: same light source, opposite visibility by day and by night
temptation: write a rule that campfires are always visible from ridges at a fixed distance

place: The same valley in daylight, clear sky, light wind.
lines: look at the valley from the ridge in daylight
outcome: In daylight the flame itself is washed out and invisible from the ridge, but a thin column of smoke rises above the trees and drifts with the wind, staying visible for as long as the fire is fed. A person unfamiliar with the valley might mistake it for low cloud, but anyone who has seen a cookfire before will know what it is.

effects: player learns a fire is in the valley
numbers: how tall the smoke column rises before it disperses

latent: whether the fire is being fed or dying down
state_after: campfire: burning, invisible by day, smoke rising
player: aware of a distant camp from smoke, not flame
stress: the signal changes sense and channel with the time of day, not the fire itself
temptation: hardcode that fires are visible by day the same way as by night, just dimmer

place: A hunting camp at night in open scrubland, a lantern hanging from a post.
outcome: A wolf circling the camp at a distance sees the lantern's glow and keeps its distance, wary of people. When the hunter notices movement and closes the lantern's shutter, the light drops to almost nothing within a few paces; the wolf, no longer able to place the camp precisely, drifts closer under cover of the dark to sniff at a food cache near the camp's edge.

numbers: how far the open lantern is visible on flat scrubland
how far the shuttered lantern still shows light
how close the wolf comes before its own caution stops it

latent: the food cache the wolf can smell but has not yet found
state_after: wolf: closer to camp, still wary
stress: shuttering removes a light-based cue but does nothing about smell or sound
temptation: make a shuttered lantern invisible outright rather than merely much dimmer

place: Open grassland at dusk, a light breeze blowing from the east.
lines: creep toward the deer from the west, staying low
outcome: Approaching from downwind of the deer, with the breeze carrying the player's scent away rather than toward it, the deer relies on sight and hearing alone and does not startle until the player is fairly close. Had the player circled to the east and approached with the wind at their back, the deer would have caught their scent long before they were in sight and bolted well out of range.

numbers: how close the player gets before the deer notices by sight or sound

latent: the deer's escape route if it does bolt
stress: wind direction alone flips a stalk from viable to hopeless
temptation: give deer a fixed detection radius that ignores wind direction

place: The same grassland, player now upwind of the deer.
lines: circle around and approach the deer from the east
outcome: With the wind now blowing from the player toward the deer, the deer catches human scent on the breeze while the player is still far off, well before any sound or sight would have given them away. It lifts its head, goes still for a moment, then runs, putting a long stretch of open ground between itself and the smell before it stops to look back.

because: agent is upwind of nothing, patient is upwind of agent
effects: deer learns a person is near
numbers: how far scent carries on a light breeze before it thins out

effects: deer moves to far side of grassland
numbers: how far the deer runs before stopping

latent: whether the deer will return to graze here later
stress: the same stalk fails outright on wind direction alone, before skill or noise enter into it
temptation: treat every stalking attempt as a single stealth roll regardless of wind

place: A farmhouse at night, a dog sleeping by the door, the household asleep inside.
outcome: A stranger easing open the farmyard gate makes almost no sound to human ears, but the dog wakes at the faint creak and the stranger's unfamiliar scent on the air, and begins barking well before anyone in the house stirs. The household wakes only once the barking has gone on for a while, by which point the stranger has already had time to slip away or to be caught in the yard.

effects: dog learns someone is at the gate
numbers: how faint a sound a sleeping dog still wakes to

effects: dog learns stranger is not household

numbers: how long the barking runs before a sleeper wakes

latent: whether the stranger meant harm or was only lost
state_after: stranger: discovered or fled, uncertain which
stress: the dog notices well ahead of the people it warns, and the warning itself takes time to land
temptation: make the dog's bark instantly wake the whole household

place: A dry forest floor thick with fallen branches, midday.
lines: move quickly through the trees toward the ridge
outcome: Moving quickly and carelessly, the player's foot comes down on a dry branch, and the snap carries clearly through the still forest air. A wild boar rooting some way off lifts its head at the sound, and though it cannot see the player through the trees, it moves off in the opposite direction rather than investigate, unwilling to risk finding out what made the noise.

numbers: how far a dry snap carries in still forest air
how far the boar withdraws

latent: how close the player actually was to the boar's wallow
stress: the boar reacts to sound alone and never confirms what caused it, so caution wins over curiosity
temptation: make every twig-snap alert every nearby creature identically regardless of what it is

place: A palisade gate at night, one guard posted, hours into a long watch.
lines: watch the guard from the treeline and time an approach
outcome: Early in the watch the guard is alert, turning to check the treeline every so often, and any approach would be seen at a fair distance in the torchlight. Well past midnight the same guard has grown drowsy, head nodding, eyes drifting shut for stretches at a time; a careful approach along the darker side of the gate now goes unnoticed until the player is close enough to touch the wall.

numbers: how far the torchlit approach is visible early in the watch
how many hours into the watch before drowsiness sets in
how close the player gets before a drowsy guard would notice

latent: whether the guard is due to be relieved soon
stress: the same sentry's reliability changes over the course of one watch without anything else changing
temptation: give a guard a single fixed perception value for the whole watch

place: A riverside camp during a steady rainstorm with gusting wind.
lines: cut the rope on the tied boat while the storm is loud
outcome: The rain drums on the boat and the tent, and the wind gusts through the reeds, and under that noise the scrape of a knife through wet rope goes unheard even a few paces away. The camp owner, dozing inside the tent with the storm as a constant backdrop, never stirs. In clear still weather the same cut would likely have carried enough to wake a light sleeper.

numbers: how loud the cutting sound is at close range

effects: camp owner loses chance to hear
numbers: how much ambient noise it takes to cover a given sound at a given distance

latent: that the boat will be found adrift only once the storm clears
stress: weather noise is a resource the player can spend a stealthy act against
temptation: give rain a flat stealth bonus number instead of it masking specific sounds by loudness and distance

place: A moor at dawn thick with fog, visibility down to a few strides.
outcome: A wolf pack working the moor's edge passes close by a traveler without either side seeing the other, the fog cutting sight to almost nothing; only the traveler's boots crunching frost-stiffened grass gives them away, and the pack veers off toward easier prey it can smell nearby rather than investigate an unseen sound. The traveler never learns how close the danger came.

because: agent is close to the ground
numbers: how far sight reaches in thick fog

effects: wolf pack learns something moves nearby

latent: how close the pack actually passed
state_after: wolf pack: moved off toward the sheep
stress: neither party ever confirms the other, and a stronger competing cue (nearby sheep) decides the outcome, not stealth
temptation: make fog simply halve a fixed detection range rather than gate sight down to a short distance

place: A snow-covered forest the morning after fresh snowfall, still air.
lines: follow the tracks leading away from the cabin
outcome: The fresh snow holds a clean line of footprints leading from the cabin door into the trees, easy to follow even for someone with little tracking skill, and it also muffles the player's own footsteps as they follow. Once the tracks reach a stretch of wind-scoured rock the trail vanishes entirely, and the player has to guess which way the thief went from the lay of the land alone.

effects: player learns which way the thief went
numbers: how old tracks can be and still show clearly in snow
how much snow depth it takes to muffle footfall

because: agent leaves no mark on stone
numbers: how far the bare rock stretch runs

latent: which direction the thief actually took past the rock
state_after: tracks: visible up to the rock, then gone
player: at a dead end, guessing
stress: the same surface that reveals one thing conceals another, and the trail simply ends rather than resolving
temptation: make tracking a single skill check with a pass or fail regardless of ground surface

place: A river gorge with steep rock walls, a bell hanging at a rope bridge crossing.
lines: ring the bell at the bridge
outcome: The bell's ring bounces off the gorge's rock walls and repeats as a fading echo, so that a lookout posted well up the gorge, who could never have heard the bell directly at that range, hears the echo rolling down the canyon and comes to investigate. The echo also makes it hard for the lookout to judge exactly where the sound came from, so they search the wrong stretch of the bridge first.

numbers: how loud the bell is at the source
how far an echo carries beyond the sound's direct range, and how many times it repeats

effects: bandit lookout learns someone rang the bell

latent: that the lookout will search the wrong stretch first
state_after: bandit lookout: alerted, searching the wrong place
stress: the gorge extends a sound's reach while degrading its precision, two separate effects from one geography
temptation: give enclosed spaces a flat noise-range multiplier without also blurring where the sound seems to come from

place: Open plains at midday, sun high, a fallen elk carcass some distance off.
outcome: The carcass has lain in the sun for the better part of a day and begun to reek, and the smell rises with the day's warmth and carries a long way over the open plains. Vultures circling far off catch the scent and drop into a slow spiral toward it long before any hyena arrives on the ground; the hyenas that do come are drawn partly by the smell and partly by the sight of circling birds, a second, visible signal layered on the first.

numbers: how long before a carcass smells strongly enough to carry far
how far carrion scent carries on open ground and how high it can be caught from
how far circling birds are visible from the ground

latent: how many scavengers converge before the day is out
stress: one signal (smell) produces a second, independently visible signal (circling birds) that draws a different audience
temptation: have carrion attract all scavenger types at once from a single fixed radius

place: A small house under search by soldiers, an infant in a back room, midday.
lines: search the house for the hidden ledger
outcome: While the player quietly searches the front room, the infant in the back begins to cry, loud enough that the mother must go quiet it, drawing one of the soldiers waiting outside to knock and ask if everything is well inside. The crying itself reveals nothing about the search, but it forces an interruption that nearly costs the player the time needed to finish before someone comes in to check.

numbers: how loud and how far a baby's crying carries through a house
how long it takes to settle a crying infant

latent: whether the soldiers will still come in to check despite the quiet
state_after: soldiers: suspicious, waiting at the door
stress: a noise unrelated to the player's own action still threatens to expose them, and settling it costs time they need
temptation: script the baby crying as a scripted story beat rather than a noise with its own cause and its own fix

place: A snowfield at dusk under a clear sky and a near-full moon.
lines: cross the snowfield in the dark cloak to reach the far treeline
outcome: The moon is bright enough to throw shadows on the snow, and the player's dark cloak, which would hide them well against bare earth or trees, stands out sharply against the pale open snowfield; a watchman on the far ridge, whose eyes are already adjusted to the moonlit dark, picks out the moving shape long before the player reaches the treeline. A white or pale wrap would have blended and likely gone unseen at the same distance.

numbers: how far a dark shape against pale snow is visible under moonlight

effects: watchman on the far ridge learns someone crosses the snowfield
watchman on the far ridge gains alarm
numbers: how long it takes eyes to adapt to moonlit dark, and how much that improves distant sight

latent: whether the watchman will raise the alarm or just keep watching
state_after: watchman on the far ridge: alerted, watching
stress: the right garment for one background is the wrong garment for another, and moonlight and dark-adaptation both raise the stakes
temptation: give cloaks a single fixed stealth bonus regardless of the background they are seen against
